basis: All four evidence commands re-run clean. I re-derived the central claim independently: scripts/check-imports.sh:39 sets SUB_PACKAGES="arbitrage portfolio tuning finance export dhlisting" (six names), while `git ls-files 'internal/domain' | awk -F/ 'NF>3{print $3}' | sort -u | wc -l` returns 25 packages. I then computed, per package, the count of non-test files importing "github.com/guarzo/slabledger/internal/domain/inventory": arbitrage 4, demand 2, dhlisting 4, dhpricing 2, export 3, finance 2, portfolio 5, psacampaign 1, tuning 1 — nine top-level packages occupying the sibling position, of which demand, dhpricing and psacampaign are outside the enforced six. `git grep -n 'domain/dhlisting' -- 'internal/domain/dhpricing/*.go'` returns three hits including two production files (service.go:7, types.go:11), and `bash scripts/check-imports.sh` still exits 0 — so the sibling-to-sibling edge is real and uncaught, exactly as claimed. On the scope question I was asked to check: the finding does NOT assert that demand->inventory, dhpricing->inventory or psacampaign->inventory are violations. Its evidence claim 4 says only that those packages 'occupy the same structural position as the six enforced siblings', its exclusions state it 'did not evaluate whether dhpricing -> dhlisting is architecturally wrong on its merits, only that the declared rule does not cover it', and it never mentions advisor->ai or advisor->scoring at all. There is no overreach to downgrade for; the finding stays inside what check-imports.sh:7-8 documents.
what_the_finding_got_wrong: Two roster errors in evidence claim 2, neither touching the conclusion. (a) The claim prose says 'internal/domain/ actually contains 24 packages'; its own pasted output lists 25, and I counted 25. (b) It names dhevents, liquidation and intelligence as 'inventory-siblings absent from the enforced list', but `git grep -rn 'domain/inventory' -- internal/domain/{dhevents,liquidation,intelligence}/` returns nothing for all three — they do not import inventory and are not siblings in the sense the rule governs. Conversely it omits internal/domain/pricing/lookup, whose adapter.go:12 does import inventory. The set of genuinely uncovered inventory-importing packages is demand, dhpricing, psacampaign (+ pricing/lookup as a sub-package), not the six it lists. A fixer deriving SUB_PACKAGES from the filesystem, as the proposed_fix directs, gets the right set regardless, so the acceptance criteria remain provable.

basis: All five evidence commands reproduce byte-for-byte (162 LOC in tuning/service.go with a one-method Service interface; 902 LOC across the four inventory tuning files; the seven Compute*/Enrich* entry points referenced from exactly one external file, internal/domain/tuning/service.go; map refs=1 amb=false for three of them). I re-derived the structural claim by a different route than the finding used: I extracted all 37 non-test top-level declarations from internal/domain/inventory/tuning*.go and grepped each one for inbound references from the rest of the package. That is a superset of the finding's three-name grep, and it surfaced coupling the finding did not disclose (below). The seam is real — the computation does live in inventory and tuning is its only computational consumer — but it is not the clean leaf the finding presents.
what_the_finding_got_wrong: Three things. (1) UNDISCLOSED MOVE BLOCKER. tuning_types.go:4 declares GradePerformance, which is a parameter type of the inventory repository port itself: internal/domain/inventory/repository_analytics.go:11 declares `GetPerformanceByGrade(ctx, campaignID) ([]GradePerformance, error)`, implemented at internal/adapters/storage/postgres/analytics_store.go:144 and mocked in internal/testutil/mocks/inventory_analytics_repo.go:15. Moving tuning_types.go wholesale would force internal/domain/inventory to import internal/domain/tuning — a cycle, since tuning already imports inventory. The exclusions disclose PurchaseWithSale and TuningResponse but not GradePerformance, so the file-level move the proposed_fix describes cannot be executed as written; tuning_types.go must be split, not moved. (2) The 'naming' category and the headline 'the package named tuning contains no tuning logic' are not supported. Package tuning exposes GetCampaignTuning returning a tuning response — the name describes what the package is about accurately. The defect is cohesion/placement, not a misleading name; nothing here meets the bar of a name describing what the code no longer does or colliding with another concept. Recategorize as architecture. (3) blast_radius omits internal/adapters/scoring/provider.go, which imports internal/domain/tuning and dereferences tuningData.MarketAlignment at :77-78, so it takes an import change too. NOT a wire break: the tuning types are JSON-tagged and mirrored at web/src/types/campaigns/analytics.ts:197-203, but a package move preserves JSON tags, so the contract survives as long as no field or type is renamed — the fixer must be told to move only.

basis: All four evidence commands reproduce (919 LOC across the four suggestion files; the inbound grep returns empty; the map records GenerateSuggestions refs=2 at portfolio/snapshot.go:228 and portfolio/service.go:306; confidenceLabelWithAge declared at inventory/portfolio.go:415 and called from suggestion_rules.go:200). All four evidence commands reproduce exactly (10,428 production LOC in inventory; 2,901 LOC in the import subsystem; 19 external consumer files for the parser entry points; sibling sizes tuning 162 / finance 207 / export 260 / portfolio 1518 / arbitrage 1244). The measurable facts are solid and I re-derived each from the commands directly. What does not survive is the causal headline.
what_the_finding_got_wrong: The title asserts causation — 'inventory is 10,428 LOC BECAUSE the flat-sibling rule makes it the only legal home for anything two siblings share' — and the finding's own largest exhibit contradicts it. The CSV-import subsystem is 2,901 LOC, 28% of the package, and it is not shared between siblings at all: evidence claim 3 shows its consumers are handlers, schedulers, clients and cmd/, i.e. adapters, none of which the flat-sibling rule constrains. The import subsystem sits in inventory for reasons unrelated to the stated cause, so the cause explains at most the smaller remainder. Evidence claim 4 shows the siblings are thin, which is consistent with the hypothesis but does not establish it — no counterfactual is offered. Separately: claim 2 says the import subsystem spans '19 files'; `git ls-files 'internal/domain/inventory/*.go' | grep -v _test | grep -cE '/(parse_|import_|service_import_|cert_import)'` returns 15. The 19 is the external-consumer count from claim 3, transposed. Scope: step 1 of the proposed fix is NB-002 and NB-003 restated, so Task 14 must cluster rather than count this separately; step 3 ('revisit the flat-sibling rule') has no acceptance criterion and is a design decision, not a ticket. Step 2 (extract internal/domain/csvimport/) is the only independently actionable and independently evidenced unit, and it is provable from acceptance criterion 2. Ticket step 2 only; severity for that unit is medium, not high.

basis: All three evidence commands reproduce. I then did the check the finding did not: I read the declarations of the *other* file, analytics_types.go, to test whether the two near-identical names actually hold different concepts. They do — analytics_types.go declares CampaignPNL, ChannelPNL, DailySpend, DaysToSellBucket, AgingItem, InventoryResult, InventorySignals, SellSheet*, CapitalTimeline, WeeklyReviewSummary, MarketSignal (genuinely analytics/reporting), while types_analytics.go declares AlertLevel, RecoveryTrend, InvoiceSellThrough, CapitalRawData, CapitalSummary, ComputeCapitalSummary, PurchaseFilter/Opt/With*, ChannelVelocity, PortfolioHealth, CampaignHealth. This clears the bar for an anchored naming defect rather than a preference: one filename describes contents it does not hold, and two files in the same directory differ only by word order while holding unrelated concepts — a concrete hazard for anyone grepping or navigating the package. The exclusion's constraint also checks out: `git grep -n '\bComputeCapitalSummary\b'` shows callers in three different siblings (arbitrage/service.go:119, finance/service.go:43, portfolio/service.go:367 and snapshot.go:249,271), so the flat-sibling rule genuinely blocks relocating it into any one of them and the finding is right to propose renaming only. BLAST RADIUS IS SAFE: these are intra-package file renames — no import path, no JSON tag, no DB column, no env var, no docs/API.md field changes. Nothing crosses a wire boundary.

Both evidence commands reproduce (service_advanced.go holds exactly LookupCert at :11 and QuickAddPurchase at :38; the cert-named files are cert_import_types.go and service_cert_entry.go). I looked for an anchor stronger than 'advanced is a vague word', and found one the finding did not cite: service_cert_entry.go:472 declares `func (s *service) ResolveCert(ctx, certNumber) (*CertInfo, error)`, while service_advanced.go:11 declares `LookupCert(ctx, certNumber) (*CertInfo, *MarketSnapshot, error)`. Two near-synonymous cert-resolution methods returning the same CertInfo type (declared at service.go:157) are split across two files, and the only thing separating them is an adjective that names no concept. That is a name misleading in this repo, not a stylistic preference. The disclosed size interaction is real: service_cert_entry.go is 491 lines against a 500-line warn / 600-line fail budget, which is why the proposed_fix's fallback (create service_cert_lookup.go rather than reintroduce an adjective) matters. Severity low and effort S are both accurate; intra-package file moves cross no wire boundary.

The evidence reproduces — but it does not establish the defect. The claim is that the filename `matching.go` is a misnomer for campaign-targeting predicates. Reading the declarations it cites: ParseRange, MatchInput, PurchaseMatchesCampaign, LanguageAxisMatches, SubjectAxisMatches, SpecDenied, MatchResult, FindMatchingCampaign. Six of the eight exported symbols contain 'Match', and two of the three types are MatchInput and MatchResult. A file named matching.go containing the matching predicates is descriptive, not misleading. None of the three anchors applies: the name does not describe something the code no longer does, it does not collide with a different concept elsewhere (`git ls-files 'internal/domain/inventory/matching*'` returns only matching.go and matching_test.go), and it is not contradicted by its own package. The third evidence item — the comment block at portfolio.go:319-326 saying a nearby check deliberately does NOT delegate to SubjectAxisMatches — is offered as proof the concept 'has already begun to fork under the generic name', but the comment reads as a deliberate design decision documented against future 'simplification', which is the opposite of drift caused by a filename. The finding also concedes the case itself: confidence `suspected`, exclusions state it is 'a rename/relocate judgment with no mechanical seam behind it', and it says the relocation cannot be actioned before the NB-004 step-3 decision. What remains is a preference for `campaign_targeting.go` over `matching.go`. Refuted under the default-to-refuted rule; a fixer could execute the rename but could not demonstrate anything was wrong before it.
what_the_finding_got_wrong: It treats a generic-but-accurate filename as a defect without evidence of anyone being misled. Its own severity of `medium` is also unsupportable for a two-file intra-package rename that the finding says cannot be actioned yet. The one substantive observation buried in the exclusions — ParseRange is a generic string helper that likely belongs in internal/platform/ — is explicitly 'not separately assessed' and so carries no evidence either.

basis: All three evidence commands reproduce, including the empty output on claim 2. I established the move's safety independently by reading the file: internal/domain/inventory/invoice_projection.go declares InvoiceProjection (four plain fields, NO struct tags) and ComputeInvoiceProjection, and depends on inventory.Invoice. Its sole consumer is internal/domain/finance/service.go:49, which assigns the four fields onto summary and branches on projection.NextInvoiceDate at :55-67. finance already imports inventory, so relocating the file creates no new sibling edge and `bash scripts/check-imports.sh` stays green. BLAST RADIUS IS SAFE: the type carries no JSON tags, so no web/src/types/ interface, no docs/API.md field, no DB column and no env var is touched — this is purely an internal package move. Severity low and effort S are right, and the proposal to bundle it with NB-002 as one 'reunite each sibling with its computation' change is sound.
what_the_finding_got_wrong: Evidence claim 2 ('InvoiceProjection itself has no consumer outside the file that declares it') is literally true but reads as stronger than it is: finance does consume the type, via `projection := inventory.ComputeInvoiceProjection(...)` at service.go:49, where type inference means the identifier never appears in the source text. The grep measures textual absence, not absence of use. The conclusion is unaffected — the consumer is finance either way, which is the package the finding proposes moving to.

basis: Both evidence commands reproduce, including the empty output. Judged as a pointer, per instruction, on whether the thing it points at is real: it is. `git grep -nE '\bSnapshotRepository\b' -- '*.go'` returns nothing at all — the symbol is declared nowhere in the repository. The eight *Repository interfaces that do exist in internal/domain/inventory are CampaignRepository, PurchaseRepository, SaleRepository, AnalyticsRepository, FinanceRepository, PricingRepository, DHRepository and PendingItemRepository (the last at pending_items.go:44). /workspace/CLAUDE.md:88 lists the first seven and then names SnapshotRepository as the eighth, and CLAUDE.md:37 repeats the '8 focused repo interfaces' count. So the count is right and exactly one name is wrong. Correctly routed to the docs-config-tests lens rather than filed as a competing finding, and the acceptance criterion (every name in the roster resolves to a `^type <Name> interface` declaration, roster count equals grep count) is directly provable. Task 14 should merge this into whatever docs-drift ticket that lens produces rather than ticket it standalone.

I verified the controller's refutation independently before recording it, and the controller is right on the facts. `git grep -nE '\b(DetectCoverageGaps|ExtractCharacter|ClassifyEra|ClassifyPriceTier)\b' -- 'internal/domain/inventory/*.go'` shows all four called from inside ComputePortfolioInsights: ExtractCharacter at portfolio.go:207 and :234, ClassifyEra at :224, ClassifyPriceTier at :229, DetectCoverageGaps at :246. ComputePortfolioInsights (portfolio.go:200) has three external call sites, all in the sibling package: internal/domain/portfolio/service.go:213, service.go:303, snapshot.go:227. CoverageGap is declared at portfolio_types.go:24, surfaced as `CoverageGaps []CoverageGap \`json:"coverageGaps"\`` at portfolio_types.go:48, and consumed by the frontend at web/src/types/campaigns/portfolio.ts:29 and :59. All five symbols are live; the cluster is reachable and serializes to the client. Not ticketable, and no removal should ever be attempted from this record. The map data the finding cites also reproduces exactly (all five refs=0 amb=false test_only=false) — the numbers are correct, the deadness inference from them is not.
what_the_finding_got_wrong: Nothing that the finding itself asserted — and the controller's paraphrase of it in ADJUDICATIONS.md overstates the claim, which the controller should know. ADJUDICATIONS.md renders the claim as 'five symbols are dead'. The finding never says that. Its title claims only that the five 'show zero external references and are unambiguous in the map' (true, and reproduced), its confidence is `suspected`, and its exclusions state outright: 'This lens did NOT run the nine runtime-reachability checks on these symbols; CoverageGap in particular carries JSON tags and could be an unreferenced-in-Go API contract (mechanism 4).' That is the exact mechanism that makes them live, named by the lens itself, before the controller found it. The verdict of refuted is still correct — the thing this pointer points at, a dead-code candidate cluster, is not real, and PREAMBLE rule 5 means a pointer that cannot survive is not worth routing — but the record should reflect that the lens hedged correctly rather than that it claimed deadness. This matters for Task 14: the lens's pointer discipline here was sound behavior to preserve, not a failure to correct.
